title: Triweekly Outcome Journal & KPI Sketch
content:
Short note: moving to a 3-week cadence for personal outcomes to match sprint + buffer weeks. Goal is to have outcome-focused check-ins that are light but measurable. Treat this doc as a scratchbook: keep hypotheses, quick metrics, and small experiments that I can run between sprints.

High-level objective (Q1-ish): reduce token-cost for inference experiments while keeping human-perceived quality stable, and free up 5 hours/week for infra ownership work.

Draft KR candidates (triweekly increments):
- KR1: Drop mean per-request token cost by 8% in the triweekly window (measure: running 7-day rolling avg on cost-center tags).
- KR2: Ship 2 small runtime optimizations (PRs merged + perf benchmark) with end-to-end tests.
- KR3: Document one rollback/fallback playbook and run one drill with SRE.
- KR4: Block time: maintain 5h/week for infra tasks (calendar blocked >= 10 of 15 working days).

This triweekly focus (week 1-3):
- Week 1: microbench param-tile batching (experiment A/B) + collect token cost per model variant.
- Week 2: integrate KV-prefix cache toggle into dev branch, add metrics to console sim.
- Week 3: run quality spot-checks against baseline prompts, write playbook notes for fallback.

Quick checks (actuals & notes):
- Week 1 snapshot: batching patch reduces per-token CPU by ~3% in synthetic runs but increases tail latency slightly. Need to tune batch timeout.
- Week 2 snapshot: KV cache toggle works but cache-hit mislabels 0.7% of requests (likely prefix hashing mismatch). Filed ticket: KPI-42 (linked).
- Week 3 snapshot: spot-checks show negligible quality drift on curated prompt-set (30 samples). Thumbs up to roll forward with canary.

Experiments and hypothesis list (fast / low-cost):
- H1: Small batching windows (8–15ms) reduce cost without hurting p95 if we keep async streaming on. Experiment: vary window in 5ms steps.
- H2: Quantize-to-8 with per-layer delay can reduce GPU memory pressure; hypothesize 6–9% cost drop for long seqs. Run on dedicated test node only.
- H3: Add cheap reranker to short-circuit long-decode paths for queries with short intents. Measure tokens saved.

Signals & metrics I actually track (notes to self on thresholds):
- Cost per 1k requests (projected 30-day rolling) — target: -8% from baseline.
- p95 latency (ms) — soft target: <= 150ms for canary traffic; hard target <= 250ms.
- Quality checks: auto-eval BLEU-ish-ish on the prompt set (not perfect); flag any drop > 1.5% for manual review.
- Calendar occupancy: count blocked hours; if <5h/week reduce meetings.

Blockers / asks (to bring up in next 1:1 / sync):
- Need SRE help to provision a dedicated test node (quota stall, reached out to Rui).
- Product: confirm we can use the canary label for ~5% production traffic for 48h.
- Legal: quick review of sample-storage retention for cached prompts (I think it's okay but want confirmation).

Concrete next actions (triweekly):
- A1: Tweak batcher timeout + push canary config by EOW (assign: me).
- A2: Pair with Amina to harden KV hashing test and write a regression test for cache labeling (assign: Amina + me).
- A3: Draft fallback playbook doc and link to console traceview (assign: me; deliverable: 1-page).

Notes to self / heuristics (voice memo style):
- Prefer small wins over big rewrites — pick 2 micro-optimizations per triweek and measure end-to-end.
- If performance improvement is <2% and increases operational complexity, deprioritize.
- Keep prompts sample set small but representative — rotate in 10 new queries every triweek.

Random ideas to revisit later:
- Could we measure quality by combining human micro-ratings (5-10 users) + automatic embedding-distance monotone checks? Low-cost panel.
- Explore a simple RL reward proxy for token-efficiency to rank model variants for routing.

Scratchpad (raw traces / short links):
- microbench script: /home/kyung/perf/microbench/batcher-test-2026-02-09.sh
- jira/linear: KPI-42 (cache mislabel), KPI-43 (canary traffic request).
- PR: recipes/pull/128 — contains batching shim prototype.

Reflections (end of triweek):
- Felt rushed week 2 — need to block deep work first two mornings.
- Collaboration was good; pair debugging with Amina shaved two days off.
- Next triweek: aim to hand off the fallback playbook to SRE for review rather than implement end-to-end myself.

End of note. Keep this as the working triweekly journal. If it gets stable, move content to personal OKR board and close action items.
